mechanism: Diphenhydramine's anticholinergic properties may reduce gastrointestinal motility and alter ferrous sulfate absorption; ferrous sulfate may cause GI upset which diphenhydramine could mask or potentiate.
action: Monitor for adequate iron absorption and GI tolerance; separate administration by 2 hours if possible; counsel patient on expected GI effects and not to rely on diphenhydramine to manage iron-related nausea without medical guidance.
